context:
Goal: a report's guard line names a real PR, commit, step or debt, so a habit is never taken for a guard (your Nov 8, 11:27 CST ruling).
Problem (rule): today's check is hardcoded: it reads only a line that starts with "Guard:", so the 11:26 CST incident's form, "The builders broke X — Guard: future briefs run the check", passes.
Based on (read): lint/report_guard.py reads a sentence-start label by pattern; the lane's 14:16 CST options; no cost below is measured.
Departs from: main reads only a guard label that starts a line — each option reads more.
home: step habit-is-not-a-guard (a report's guard line names a real guard)

options.gain: Closes the incident's form; same cost as today, no model call.
options.how: The check also reads "Missing guard:", "(Guard: ...)" and a label after a dash, comma or "and". A paraphrase with no word "guard" still passes; a judge comes later only if one slips through.
options.label: More label forms (Recommended)
options.lose: Still a word list; a paraphrase passes.

options.how: Any sentence holding "guard", in any section, must name a PR, commit, step or debt.
options.label: Any sentence with the word guard
options.lose: False alarms on ordinary lines such as "the push guard refused it"; a paraphrase still passes.

options.gain: Catches a paraphrase; no word list.
options.how: A model reads each landed report and flags a line that claims a prevention with no reference.
options.label: A judge reads meaning
options.lose: A model call on every report; results can differ run to run, so it cannot be proven red on a fixed case.
